title: Polylight SDK handoff kit & boot protocol (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, time-boxed handoff kit for engineers and SEs to take an embedder/SDK integration from clone -> instrumented demo in 30 minutes. It assumes the target is a small sample app (React or Node CLI) that calls Redwood’s hosted SDK endpoints. The focus is developer experience: low friction, deterministic telemetry, and safe defaults for canarying.

Audience:
- Solutions engineers doing customer demos
- SDK maintainers running quick verification or triage
- New hires (engineer/SE) who need a predictable first-run ritual

What this is NOT:
- A full onboarding curriculum (see confluence link)
- A security or legal checklist (eng-security owns that)

Quick path (30-minute end-to-end):
1) Pre-reqs (5m):
- Repo: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/example-embedder.git
- Local env: node 18+, npm/yarn; have REDWOOD_API_KEY in env (dev token)
- Confirm network access to api.redwood.ai (or set local proxy)

2) Wire-up (10m):
- Install SDK: npm install @redwood/sdk-lite
- Replace sample prompt in /examples/basic-demo.js with a short test prompt: "Summarize: Redwood is..."
- Run: node examples/basic-demo.js and confirm response returns streaming chunks within ~300–700ms.

3) Instrumentation + telemetry (8m):
- Enable lightweight telemetry wrapper: set RW_TELEM=on in .env (default in kit)
- Confirm events: first_call, token_usage, latency_ms in the demo UI (http://localhost:6006/telemetry)
- Add tags: sdk_version and env=dev so we can filter in Console dashboards

4) Canary + rollback smoke (7m):
- Route sample traffic to a canary model via env var CANARY_MODEL=redwood-small-v2-canary
- Run a 2-minute burst (ab -n 50 -c 5 or local pump script)
- Verify fallbacks: if canary latency > 1s or errors > 3%, abort and set CANARY_MODEL=stable-default

Minimal example snippets for quick copy-paste:
- Node (basic):
const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk-lite');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
(async () => {
  const resp = await client.generate({ model: process.env.CANARY_MODEL || 'redwood-small-v1', prompt: 'Summarize Redwood in one sentence' });
  console.log(resp.text);
})();

- cURL (sanity):
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-small-v1","prompt":"tokenize this"}'

Telemetry expectations and checks:
- Required fields emitted on first call: request_id, sdk_version, model, prompt_hash (sha1), latency_ms.
- Secondary metrics (optional): token_in, token_out, kv_cache_hit_rate.
- If any required field is missing, fail fast: the locally-run telemetry UI surfaces a red banner.

Opinionated defaults in the kit (rationale included):
- timeout 5s for first-byte, overall 20s (protects demos from waiting forever).
- batch_size: 1 in dev (avoid batching surprise latency), 16 in CI/load tests
- streaming enabled by default (better demo sightlines)
- retry policy: exponential backoff up to 2 retries only (avoid cascading load)

Handoff checklist for SDK maintainers / SEs (short):
- [ ] Confirm SDK release tag referenced in example matches published package
- [ ] Verify telemetry pipeline shows the required fields for the demo token
- [ ] Smoke test canary route and validate fallback policy behavior
- [ ] Update quickstart README with any transient workarounds (e.g., proxy config)

Notes to self / open questions (working):
- Should the demo default to a private-deploy placeholder if REDWOOD_API_KEY missing? (tradeoff: less friction vs. leaking hostnames)
- Can we bake a one-click Cloud Shell link that pre-populates env vars for faster SE onboarding?
- Need a reliable short TTL demo token for shared demo accounts; coordinate with infra billing.

Edge-case debug tips (copyable):
- If streaming stalls: check for TCP windowing / network middlebox; run a curl with --raw and inspect chunk boundaries.
- If telemetry missing request_id: confirm the SDK wrapper is invoked before any network middleware that might swallow headers.
- If canary flips but latency remains high: consider quantized model variant or smaller sequence length for demo prompts.

Appendix: local pump script (single-file)
- The repo includes /scripts/pump-demo.js which runs parallel requests and outputs a summary (latency p50/p95, errors). Use it for the quick canary burst.

Who to ping:
- SDK owner: @jared.liu (collaborator)
- DX lead: maya.thompson@redwood.ai
- Infra for demo tokens: infra-billing@redwood.ai

Revision log:
- 2024-11-05: initial sketch and checklist (Maya)
- 2024-12-10: added telemetry expectations and pump script hint (Jared)

End of draft.

-- small, modular, copy-friendly: keep this doc a single-screen checklist SEs can follow during live demos.
